messages:
Alex: Heads-up: proposing we decouple 'residency' (strong local ownership) from 'warmup' (prefetch/warm) in the prefix cache API. We've been folding both into the Lease/Pin surface and it's making eviction math and correctness reasoning awkward.

Alex: Intent: Ownership/residency = a correctness and read-liveness primitive (you can serve reads locally while token valid). Warmup/prefetch = an advisory signal to reduce cold misses; not relied on for correctness.

Jamie: I like the separation. Quick clarifying question: will reads be allowed with only a warmup present? or must ownership be held?

Alex: Reads require ownership for guaranteed local serve. Warmup can be used opportunistically if the block happens to be resident, but it is explicitly not a guarantee.

Priya: Eviction consequence: we must ensure warmup entries are first-class citizens in the eviction scoring but with much lower retention priority. Otherwise noisy warmups will evict true owners. Suggest scoring: owner_weight >> recent_access_weight >> warmup_weight.

Sven: Agree. Implementation detail: give warmups a soft TTL and a churn score. On memory pressure we preferentially evict warmups by increasing their decay factor. Ownership tokens are treated as protective pins (except during handoff).

Alex: API sketch (informal):
```
// residency API
AcquireResidency(prefix_id, reason) -> ResidencyToken
ReleaseResidency(prefix_id, token)

// warmup API
WarmupPrefix(prefix_id, {priority: LOW|MED|HIGH, hint_expires_ms})

// ResidencyToken (opaque but small): {lease_id, epoch, tenant_id}
```
ResidencyToken contains epoch and lease id to validate handoffs. Tokens must be tenant-scoped.

Jamie: Handoff race handling? we've seen races when two nodes try to take the same prefix.

Sven: Proposal: two-phase handoff with epoch checks and atomic residency swap on the metadata row. Pseudocode:
1) Receiver writes a pending_claim record with new_lease_id and expected_epoch.
2) Owner validates its epoch and attempts an atomic compare-and-swap to update the resident lease_id to new_lease_id.
3) If CAS succeeds, receiver marks residency active. If not, receiver aborts and triggers conservative fallback.

If any step sees epoch drift, we fall back to remote fetch and emit a metric. No silent correctness shortcuts.

Priya: Metrics to surface (tenant tagged): residency.hit, residency.miss, warmup.request, warmup.evicted, warmup.wasted_bytes, eviction.reclaimed_bytes, read.latency.owner_hit, read.latency.cold_miss. Ops needs histograms for latency and counters for wasted warmup.

Alex: Feature-flag + migration plan: implement new APIs and provide a compatibility shim (legacy AcquireAndWarm => AcquireResidency + Warmup). Rollout via feature flag OFF by default: 10% traffic for 24h, evaluate metrics, 50% next 48h, then 100%.
Provide an explicit rollback knob and a per-tenant opt-out. Persisted lease rows get new columns residency_epoch and warmup_meta (optional). New servers read both; old servers ignore warmup_meta.

Jamie: Tests: unit tests for contested AcquireResidency, integration test for handoff under node restarts, canary that simulates 1k hotkeys with varying warmup aggressiveness. Also validate the compatibility shim with old SDKs.

Priya: Security: ResidencyToken must be bound to tenant_id and validated. Also audit logs for token issuance/handback. Debug endpoints that list active residency tokens should be read-only and RBAC-protected.

Sven: Backpressure: when node memory usage > threshold, drop pending warmups and start decaying warmup_score faster. Also rate-limit warmup requests per-tenant by a configurable token-bucket.

Alex: API ergonomics: ResidencyToken should be cacheable locally (no per-read RPC). Warmup should accept batches: WarmupPrefix([p1,p2,p3], priority). Keep token representation compact (16-32 bytes).

InfraBot: deploy-bot: created canary group "prefix-residency-warmup-canary" in eng-runtime-alpha; will route initial 10% traffic.

Jamie: Ops playbook: if warmup.wasted_bytes or warmup.evicted spikes after rollout, immediately throttle warmup_priority and check tenant warmup quotas. If residency.miss rate increases, roll back feature flag.

Priya: Action items: Alex -> RFC + API spec + migration runbook (Friday EOD). Jamie -> metrics dashboard + alert thresholds (Mon). Sven -> handoff state machine doc + failure scenarios (Tue). Priya -> canary test harness + e2e scenarios (next Wed).

Alex: I'll include an example debug endpoint: GET /debug/node/{id}/residency -> list of {prefix_id, lease_id, epoch, tenant_id, held_since}. Authz enforced. Will also add a small CLI for offline inspection.

Sven: Minor note: document explicitly why warmup != implicit residency (eviction semantics, predictable memory accounting, simpler handoff). I'll draft a short section in the RFC.

Alex: Thanks team. I'll open the RFC PR and link to the canary dashboard when deployed. Ping me if you want to pair on the handoff tests.

InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary "prefix-residency-warmup-canary" started at 10% traffic; logs forwarded to /canary/prefix-residency-warmup (streaming).
